references.text: The scarlet cord reminds us of the blood on the doorposts during the Passover in Egypt, which protected the Israelite families from the angel of death.
Hyssop and blood on the doorposts as a sign of protection parallel the scarlet cord as a sign of salvation for Rahab's family.
The fulfillment of the promise given to Rahab, where she and her entire household were saved from the destruction of Jericho.
Confirmation that Rahab and her father's house were spared, just as the spies had promised.
Lot was told to gather his whole family in the house before the destruction of Sodom, in the same way Rahab was to gather her family.
Rahab's faith is mentioned in Hebrews as an example of saving faith that rescued her from destruction.
James mentions Rahab as an example of faith demonstrated through actions, including welcoming the spies.
Rahab is listed in Jesus' genealogy, showing that she was incorporated into the people of Israel and the lineage of the Messiah.
